questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: What is the adult sublingual nitroglycerin dose for chest pain/ACS/STEMI?
questions.explanation: The SL tablet is the first-line adult dose for chest pain/ACS/STEMI, pulmonary edema and aortic emergencies, repeatable q3 min. The infusion, the 400 mcg bolus and the 50 mcg IV dose are separate entries on the same page for different situations.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: What systolic blood pressure must be present before giving sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain?
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin is a venodilator that drops preload, so the formulary sets an SBP floor of >100 mmHg for the SL route. The >90 figure belongs to the infusion target and the >120 figure to the IV bolus.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: At what rate does an adult nitroglycerin infusion for chest pain/ACS start?
questions.explanation: The infusion begins at 10 mcg/min and is titrated for pain while maintaining an SBP > 90. 400 mcg/min is the ceiling, not the starting point.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: What is the maximum rate of an adult nitroglycerin infusion?
questions.explanation: Titration for pain and SBP > 90 is capped at 400 mcg/min. Above that the guideline offers no further nitroglycerin titration.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: What is the adult nitroglycerin dose for uterine inversion?
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin is used as a uterine relaxant to permit replacement of an inverted uterus, and that indication carries its own single 50 mcg IV dose rather than the cardiac dosing.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: An adult with pulmonary edema has continued dyspnea. What is the adult nitroglycerin IV bolus dose?
options: 10 mcg over 2 minutes via IV pump
50 mcg over 2 minutes via IV pump
100 mcg over 2 minutes via IV pump
400 mcg over 2 minutes via IV pump
questions.explanation: Continued dyspnea from pulmonary edema is the trigger for the high-dose bolus: 400 mcg over 2 minutes via IV pump, on top of any running infusion.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: How often may the adult 400 mcg nitroglycerin bolus be repeated, and to what total?
options: Every 2 minutes, to a total of 3 doses
Every 3 minutes, to a total of 3 doses
Every 5 minutes, to a total of 3 doses
Every 5 minutes, to a total of 2 doses
questions.explanation: The bolus may be repeated q5 min for a total of 3 doses. The q3 min interval belongs to the SL tablet, not the IV bolus.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: What systolic blood pressure is required before the 400 mcg nitroglycerin IV bolus is given?
questions.explanation: The bolus carries a higher pressure requirement than the SL tablet because 400 mcg over 2 minutes drops preload abruptly; SBP must be >120.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: Which phosphodiesterase inhibitor bars nitroglycerin if taken within the previous 24 hours (rather than the 48-hour window)?
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin has two exclusion windows: sildenafil within 24 hours, and vardenafil or tadalafil within 48 hours. Combining either with a nitrate can produce profound, refractory hypotension.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of nitroglycerin?
questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin is classed simply as a vasodilator; it relaxes vascular smooth muscle, reducing both preload and afterload and thus myocardial oxygen demand.

questions.title: Nitroglycerin
questions.stem: Which of these is an adverse reaction to nitroglycerin?
questions.explanation: The listed adverse reactions are hypotension, tachycardia, headache, blurred vision and vertigo. Tissue necrosis belongs to norepinephrine, uterine rupture to oxytocin and extrapyramidal symptoms to the antiemetics.

questions.title: Nitroprusside
questions.stem: What is the adult starting dose of a nitroprusside infusion for hypertension?
questions.explanation: Nitroprusside starts low at 0.3 mcg/kg/min because it is an immediate-onset arterial and venous dilator; 10 mcg/kg/min is the ceiling, not a starting point.

questions.title: Nitroprusside
questions.stem: What is the maximum nitroprusside infusion rate for hypertension?
questions.explanation: Titration stops at 10 mcg/kg/min. The ceiling matters because prolonged or high-dose infusion is the setting in which cyanide toxicity develops.

questions.title: Nitroprusside
questions.stem: How is a nitroprusside infusion titrated toward the target blood pressure?
questions.explanation: Titration mirrors the starting dose: 0.3 mcg/kg/min increments every 3-5 minutes, which matches the drug's 1-2 minute peak effect.

questions.title: Nitroprusside
questions.stem: Which diluent is required for a nitroprusside infusion?
questions.explanation: Nitroprusside must be mixed with D5W only; the recommended mixture is 50 mg in 250 mL. Mixing in saline or Ringer's is outside the guideline.

questions.title: Nitroprusside
questions.stem: What handling precaution applies once nitroprusside is mixed?
options: Infuse through a large, stable vein to avoid necrosis
Give boluses via IV pump rather than IV push
Protect from light with foil or other opaque material
Dilute to no greater than 25 mg/mL before infusing
questions.explanation: Nitroprusside degrades on light exposure, so the bag must be shielded with foil or other opaque material. The other precautions listed belong to norepinephrine, propofol and promethazine.

questions.title: Nitroprusside
questions.stem: Which toxicity is associated with prolonged or high-dose nitroprusside administration?
questions.explanation: Nitroprusside metabolism releases cyanide, so prolonged or high-dose infusion risks cyanide toxicity — the reason the 10 mcg/kg/min ceiling and duration matter on a long transport.

questions.title: Nitroprusside
questions.stem: Which condition is a contraindication to nitroprusside?
questions.explanation: Where hypertension is compensatory — an AV shunt or coarctation of the aorta — lowering the pressure removes the perfusion the lesion depends on. Inadequate cerebral circulation is the other listed contraindication.

questions.title: Norepinephrine
questions.stem: What is the adult non-weight-based starting range for a norepinephrine infusion in hypotension/shock?
questions.explanation: Adult norepinephrine is dosed two ways: 2-10 mcg/min, or weight-based at 0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min. Either is titrated q3-5 min to patient response.

questions.title: Norepinephrine
questions.stem: What is the pediatric norepinephrine dose for hypotension/shock?
questions.explanation: Pediatric dosing is the same weight-based range the adult column offers, 0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min, titrated q3-5 min. 0.25-5 mcg/kg/min is phenylephrine and 0.3 mcg/kg/min is nitroprusside.

questions.title: Norepinephrine
questions.stem: What is the listed maximum norepinephrine infusion rate for hypotension/shock?
questions.explanation: Both the adult and pediatric columns cap at 45 mcg/min. 10 mcg/min is the top of the adult starting range and 400 mcg/min is the nitroglycerin ceiling.

questions.title: Norepinephrine
questions.stem: How often is a norepinephrine infusion titrated to patient response?
questions.explanation: Titration is q3-5 min in both columns, which fits the drug's 1-3 minute onset and 5 minute peak — faster titration stacks doses before the previous one has peaked.

questions.title: Norepinephrine
questions.stem: Which of these is an adverse reaction to norepinephrine?
questions.explanation: Norepinephrine's alpha-driven rise in afterload triggers a baroreceptor-mediated reflex bradycardia; hypertension and tissue necrosis with extravasation are the other listed reactions.

questions.title: Norepinephrine
questions.stem: When may the norepinephrine maximum of 45 mcg/min be exceeded?
options: After additional vasopressors have been administered
After two crystalloid boluses have been given
Only once a central line is established
questions.explanation: The special considerations permit exceeding 45 mcg/min once additional vasopressors are on board — the ceiling applies to norepinephrine used alone, not to a multi-pressor patient.

questions.title: Norepinephrine
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of norepinephrine?
options: Nonselective alpha and beta agonist, bronchodilator
questions.explanation: Norepinephrine is classed as an alpha and beta agonist with inotropic effect; it acts predominantly on alpha receptors with slight beta-1 cardiac stimulation. Pure alpha-1 activity describes phenylephrine.

questions.title: Octreotide
questions.stem: What is octreotide indicated for?
questions.explanation: Octreotide's single formulary indication is esophageal varices; by suppressing splanchnic vasodilatory peptides it reduces portal pressure and variceal bleeding.

questions.title: Octreotide
questions.stem: What is the adult octreotide bolus dose for esophageal varices?
questions.explanation: The bolus is 25-50 mcg given slow IVP, followed by an infusion. Note the unit: this drug is dosed in micrograms, not milligrams.

questions.title: Octreotide
questions.stem: What octreotide infusion follows the bolus in esophageal varices?
questions.explanation: The bolus is followed by a 25-50 mcg/hr infusion, because variceal bleeding requires sustained suppression of splanchnic flow rather than a single dose.

questions.title: Octreotide
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of octreotide?
questions.explanation: Octreotide is a somatostatin analog; it suppresses gastrin, insulin, glucagon, secretin and motilin, which is why both hypo- and hyperglycemia appear among its adverse effects.

questions.title: Octreotide
questions.stem: Which metabolic derangement can octreotide cause?
questions.explanation: Because octreotide suppresses both insulin and glucagon, glucose can move in either direction — check a glucose during transport rather than assuming one effect.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: What is the adult ondansetron dose for nausea/vomiting?
questions.explanation: Adults get 4 mg IV/IM, repeatable once after 15 minutes; 8 mg is the total ceiling over 8 hours, not a single dose. 12.5 mg is the low end of promethazine.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: What is the maximum total adult ondansetron dose, and over what period?
questions.explanation: The adult ceiling is a total of 8 mg q8 hours — effectively the initial 4 mg plus one repeat. Exceeding it adds QT risk without added antiemetic benefit.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: What is the pediatric ondansetron dose for nausea/vomiting?
questions.explanation: Pediatric dosing is 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM, repeatable once after 15 minutes, with a 4 mg single-dose ceiling. 0.5 mg/kg is the pediatric promethazine dose.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: What is the maximum single pediatric dose of ondansetron?
questions.explanation: Even a large child is capped at 4 mg per dose, which is the adult single dose; 8 mg is the adult 8-hour total.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: After an initial dose of ondansetron, when and how many times may it be repeated?
questions.explanation: Both the adult and pediatric columns allow a single repeat after 15 minutes. Beyond that the adult is held to the 8 mg q8 hour total and the child to a 4 mg single-dose maximum.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: Which ECG finding is a contraindication to ondansetron?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron prolongs the QT, so a QTc already over 500 ms is a contraindication. The QRS and heart rate thresholds listed are sodium bicarbonate triggers in TCA overdose.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of ondansetron?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron is a selective 5-HT3 antagonist acting at the chemoreceptor trigger zone and on vagal afferents — a different mechanism from promethazine, which is an H1 blocker.

questions.title: Ondansetron
questions.stem: What limitation applies to ondansetron's effectiveness?
options: It is more effective given IM than IV
It is less effective for active vomiting than for nausea
It should only be given after promethazine has failed
It loses effect entirely if repeated
questions.explanation: Ondansetron works best to prevent or treat current nausea and is not as effective once the patient is actively vomiting — a reason to give it early in transport rather than waiting.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: What is the adult oxytocin concentration for postpartum, breech or vertex delivery?
questions.explanation: Routine post-delivery management uses the lower-strength bag, 20 units in 1000 mL of NS or LR. The 40 unit bag is reserved for hemorrhage and for uterine inversion.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: How is the 20 units/1000 mL oxytocin bag run after a vertex delivery?
questions.explanation: The routine delivery bag is run 500 mL wide open, then at 100 mL/hr to facilitate delivery of the placenta. The 10-minute/50 mL-hr scheme belongs to the 40 unit hemorrhage bag.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: What is the adult oxytocin concentration for postpartum hemorrhage?
questions.explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage, and uterine contraction after replacement of an inverted uterus, use the double-strength 40 units/1000 mL bag.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: How is the 40 units/1000 mL oxytocin bag run in postpartum hemorrhage?
questions.explanation: The hemorrhage bag is given as 500 mL over 10 minutes, then 50 mL/hr to facilitate delivery of the placenta — a controlled loading dose rather than wide open.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: In postpartum hemorrhage with no IV access available, what oxytocin dose is given?
questions.explanation: If no IV is available, 10 units IM substitutes for the infusion. It is the only IM dose listed for oxytocin.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: Which condition is a contraindication to oxytocin?
questions.explanation: A hypertonic uterus, significant cephalopelvic disproportion, fetal distress where delivery is not imminent, and any case where vaginal delivery is contraindicated all bar oxytocin. The other three options are indications for it.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: Which of these is an adverse reaction to oxytocin?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin drives sustained uterine contraction, so uterine rupture is a listed risk alongside nausea, vomiting and hypertension.

questions.title: Oxytocin
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of oxytocin?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is a pituitary hormone and uterine stimulant; it raises intracellular calcium in uterine smooth muscle, mimicking spontaneous labor contractions.

questions.title: Phenobarbital
questions.stem: What is the phenobarbital dose for status epilepticus?
questions.explanation: Status epilepticus is loaded at 15-20 mg/kg IV, and the pediatric column is the same as adult. The load is far larger than a maintenance anticonvulsant dose.

questions.title: Phenobarbital
questions.stem: At what rate is the phenobarbital load for status epilepticus infused?
questions.explanation: The load is infused at 60 mg/min. Rate control matters because a rapid barbiturate push produces hypotension and respiratory depression.

questions.title: Phenobarbital
questions.stem: What is the maximum phenobarbital dose for status epilepticus?
questions.explanation: The 15-20 mg/kg load is capped at 1000 mg, which a patient reaches at roughly 50-65 kg — so most adults are dose-capped rather than weight-dosed.

questions.title: Phenobarbital
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of phenobarbital?
questions.explanation: Phenobarbital is an anticonvulsant barbiturate; it alters sensory cortex, cerebellar and motor activity and produces sedation, hypnosis and anesthesia at increasing doses.

questions.title: Phenobarbital
questions.stem: Which paradoxical reaction can phenobarbital cause in pediatric patients?
questions.explanation: Children may respond paradoxically with agitation and hyperactivity rather than sedation, so a more awake child after phenobarbital is not evidence the dose was missed.

questions.title: Phenobarbital
questions.stem: What is the listed duration of effect of phenobarbital?
questions.explanation: Phenobarbital's onset is 5 minutes but its duration exceeds 6 hours — the loaded patient will stay sedated well past the transport, which matters for airway planning and handoff.

questions.title: Phenylephrine
questions.stem: What is the phenylephrine infusion dose for shock/hypotension?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine runs at 0.25-5 mcg/kg/min, and the pediatric column is the same as adult. 0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min is norepinephrine and 0.3 mcg/kg/min is nitroprusside.

questions.title: Phenylephrine
questions.stem: What is the maximum phenylephrine infusion rate for shock/hypotension?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine is capped at 200 mcg/minute. The 45 mcg/min figure is the norepinephrine ceiling — do not carry one pressor's maximum over to another.

questions.title: Phenylephrine
questions.stem: What is the recommended mixture for a phenylephrine infusion?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine is mixed 20 mg in 250 mL. The 4 mg/250 mL bag is norepinephrine, 50 mg/250 mL is nitroglycerin or nitroprusside, and 1000 mg/100 mL is propofol.

questions.title: Phenylephrine
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of phenylephrine?
options: Nonselective alpha and beta agonist, bronchodilator
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine is a pure alpha-1 agonist, so it raises afterload without inotropy or chronotropy — which is why it is a poor choice when the problem is pump failure.

questions.title: Phenylephrine
questions.stem: Which condition is listed under warnings and precautions for phenylephrine?
questions.explanation: Raising afterload in a failing left ventricle worsens pulmonary edema, and phenylephrine also carries warnings for myocardial infarction and tachy- or ventricular arrhythmias.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: An adult in DKA has a potassium of 4.8. How much potassium chloride, if any, is added to maintenance fluids?
options: Add KCl 20 mEq/L to maintenance fluids
Add KCl 40 mEq/L to maintenance fluids
Do not add KCl to maintenance fluids
questions.explanation: A potassium of 4.0-5.4 in adult DKA gets 20 mEq/L added to NS, D5NS or D5 half NS. Insulin therapy will drive potassium intracellularly, so replacement starts before the level falls.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: An adult in DKA has a potassium of 3.2. How much potassium chloride, if any, is added to maintenance fluids?
options: Do not add KCl to maintenance fluids
Add KCl 10 mEq/L to maintenance fluids
Add KCl 20 mEq/L to maintenance fluids
Add KCl 40 mEq/L to maintenance fluids
questions.explanation: A potassium below 4.0 in adult DKA doubles the additive to 40 mEq/L in NS, D5NS or D5 half NS, because insulin will drop it further.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: In DKA, above what potassium level is no potassium chloride added to maintenance fluids?
questions.explanation: A potassium greater than 5.4 means no KCl is added, in both the adult and pediatric columns. Adding potassium to an already hyperkalemic DKA patient risks arrest.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: A pediatric DKA patient has a potassium of 4.8. How much potassium chloride, if any, is added to maintenance fluids?
options: Add KCl 20 mEq/L to maintenance fluids
Add KCl 40 mEq/L to maintenance fluids
Do not add KCl to maintenance fluids
questions.explanation: The pediatric column uses a single band: any potassium at or below 5.4 gets 40 mEq/L added, where an adult at that level would get only 20 mEq/L.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: What is the maximum KCl infusion rate for a pediatric DKA patient?
questions.explanation: Pediatric KCl is limited to 0.5 mEq/kg/hr with an absolute ceiling of 10 mEq/hr, so a larger child does not exceed the peripheral-line limit.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: What is the adult oral KCl dose for hypokalemia?
questions.explanation: Adults get 40 mEq PO, repeatable once after 30-60 minutes if the potassium is 2.5-3.0. The weight-based 2 mEq/kg figure is the pediatric oral dose.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: What is the adult IV KCl dose for hypokalemia?
options: 40 mEq IV, not to exceed 10 mEq/hr
40 mEq IV, not to exceed 20 mEq/hr
20 mEq IV, not to exceed 10 mEq/hr
questions.explanation: The adult IV replacement dose is 40 mEq run no faster than 10 mEq/hr. The 0.5 mEq/kg over 1-2 hours figure is the pediatric IV dose.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: What is the pediatric oral KCl dose for hypokalemia?
questions.explanation: Children get 2 mEq/kg PO with an absolute cap of 40 mEq — the adult dose — repeatable once after 30-60 minutes.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: Below what potassium level is IV potassium chloride replacement given to an asymptomatic hypokalemic patient?
questions.explanation: IV replacement is reserved for a potassium under 2.5 if the patient is asymptomatic, or under 3.0 if symptomatic — symptoms move the threshold up.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: What is the maximum KCl infusion rate through a peripheral line?
questions.explanation: A peripheral line is limited to 10 mEq/hr; a central line permits 20 mEq/hr. Faster peripheral infusion causes severe infusion-site pain and vein damage.

questions.title: Potassium Chloride
questions.stem: Which route of potassium chloride administration is prohibited outright?
questions.explanation: Potassium is never given IV push — a bolus of concentrated potassium causes cardiac arrest. It must be diluted and infused, or given orally.

questions.title: Pralidoxime
questions.stem: What is the adult pralidoxime dose for organophosphate insecticide poisoning?
questions.explanation: Adults get 1-2 grams IV mixed in 100 mL NS and infused over 15-30 minutes. 20-50 mg/kg is the pediatric figure.

questions.title: Pralidoxime
questions.stem: Over what period is pralidoxime infused for organophosphate insecticide poisoning?
questions.explanation: Both columns specify an infusion over 15-30 minutes; rapid administration causes tachycardia, hypertension and laryngospasm. Onset of effect is roughly 10 minutes.

questions.title: Pralidoxime
questions.stem: What is the pediatric pralidoxime dose for organophosphate insecticide poisoning?
questions.explanation: Children get 20-50 mg/kg as an infusion in 100 mL NS over 15-30 minutes, with dose and volume not to exceed the adult dosage.

questions.title: Pralidoxime
questions.stem: A patient has organophosphate NERVE AGENT poisoning. How is the pralidoxime dose determined?
options: Give 1 - 2 grams IV in 100 mL NS
Refer to the Poisoning and Overdose PCG
questions.explanation: For nerve agent exposure the dose depends on route and presenting symptoms, so the formulary sends the crew to the Poisoning and Overdose PCG rather than giving a fixed number.

questions.title: Pralidoxime
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of pralidoxime?
questions.explanation: Pralidoxime is an organophosphate antidote; it reactivates cholinesterase mainly outside the CNS, relieving the twitching and respiratory muscle paralysis that atropine alone does not fix.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: What is the adult promethazine dose for nausea/vomiting?
questions.explanation: Adults get 12.5-50 mg by deep IM or IV, repeatable q4 hours. 0.5 mg/kg is the pediatric dose and 4 mg is ondansetron.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: How often may an adult promethazine dose be repeated for nausea/vomiting?
questions.explanation: Promethazine repeats q4 hours, matching its 4-6 hour duration. The 15 minute repeat interval belongs to ondansetron.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: What concentration and rate limits apply when promethazine is given IV?
options: No greater than 50 mg/mL, at a rate under 25 mg/min
No greater than 25 mg/mL, at a rate under 50 mg/min
No greater than 12.5 mg/mL, at a rate under 25 mg/min
No greater than 25 mg/mL, at a rate under 25 mg/min
questions.explanation: IV promethazine must be diluted to no more than 25 mg/mL and pushed at less than 25 mg/min, because concentrated or fast administration causes severe tissue injury if it extravasates.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: What is the pediatric promethazine dose for nausea/vomiting?
options: 0.1 mg/kg deep IM or IV, max 25 mg
0.5 mg/kg deep IM or IV, max 25 mg
0.5 mg/kg deep IM or IV, max 50 mg
2 mg/kg deep IM or IV, max 25 mg
questions.explanation: Children over 2 years get 0.5 mg/kg deep IM or IV with a 25 mg ceiling — half the adult maximum.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: Which patient group is a contraindication to promethazine?
questions.explanation: Promethazine is contraindicated under 2 years of age because of fatal respiratory depression in that group; the pediatric dose column repeats the restriction.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: A patient develops a dystonic reaction after promethazine. Which drug is used to treat it?
questions.explanation: Dystonic reactions are treated with diphenhydramine (Benadryl), whose anticholinergic effect counters the extrapyramidal blockade promethazine produces.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: In which patients should the promethazine dose be reduced?
options: The elderly and those already on sedating medications
Patients with a history of seizures
Patients in the first trimester of pregnancy
questions.explanation: Dose is reduced in the elderly and in patients receiving other sedating medications or with recent alcohol use, because over-sedation is the principal risk.

questions.title: Promethazine
questions.stem: Which of these is an adverse reaction to promethazine?
questions.explanation: Over-sedation, extrapyramidal symptoms, dystonia and delirium are the listed reactions — all consequences of its central dopaminergic and anticholinergic blockade.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: What is the adult propofol bolus used to initiate post-intubation sedation?
questions.explanation: An adult starting propofol gets a 1 mg/kg bolus via pump before the infusion begins. The flat 10-20 mg bolus is for a patient already on propofol who is under-sedated.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: What is the maximum adult propofol initiation bolus?
questions.explanation: The 1 mg/kg bolus is capped at 25 mg, so anyone over 25 kg is dose-capped. 20 mg is the pediatric bolus cap.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: At what rate does the propofol infusion start for post-intubation sedation?
questions.explanation: Both adult and pediatric infusions start at 25 mcg/kg/min after the bolus; 75 mcg/kg/min is the ceiling and 10 mcg/kg/min is the increment for titration.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: What is the maximum propofol infusion rate for post-intubation sedation?
questions.explanation: Both columns cap the infusion at 75 mcg/kg/min. Reaching the ceiling without adequate sedation points to missing analgesia rather than more propofol.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: What is the pediatric propofol bolus for post-intubation sedation?
options: 1 mg/kg via IV pump, max 25 mg
1 mg/kg via IV pump, max 20 mg
0.5 mg/kg via IV pump, max 25 mg
0.5 mg/kg via IV pump, max 20 mg
questions.explanation: Children get half the adult bolus, 0.5 mg/kg, capped at 20 mg — and the same bolus is used if an already-infusing child is inadequately sedated.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: An adult already receiving a propofol infusion remains inadequately sedated. What is the next step?
options: Bolus 10-20 mg via IV pump, then increase the rate by 10 mcg/kg/min
Bolus 1 mg/kg via IV pump, then increase the rate by 25 mcg/kg/min
Increase the rate by 25 mcg/kg/min without a bolus
Bolus 0.5 mg/kg via IV pump, then increase the rate by 10 mcg/kg/min
questions.explanation: For a patient already on propofol, the guideline uses a flat 10-20 mg bolus via pump followed by a 10 mcg/kg/min rate increase, still capped at 75 mcg/kg/min.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: Which allergy is a contraindication to propofol?
questions.explanation: Propofol is formulated in a lipid emulsion containing egg lecithin and soybean oil, so hypersensitivity to eggs or soy — as well as to the drug itself — is a contraindication.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: How must a propofol IV bolus be delivered?
options: By slow IV push over 2 minutes
questions.explanation: Propofol boluses must be given via pump, not IV push — the controlled delivery limits the apnea and hypotension the drug reliably causes.

questions.title: Propofol
questions.stem: Why is analgesia usually required alongside propofol?
options: Propofol shortens the duration of opioids
questions.explanation: Propofol sedates but does not treat pain, so adding analgesia both treats the patient and generally allows a lower propofol infusion rate and less hypotension.

questions.title: Racemic Epinephrine
questions.stem: What is the racemic epinephrine dose for asthma or croup?
options: 0.5 mL of 2.25% solution diluted in 2.5 mL NS
0.25 mL of 2.25% solution diluted in 2.5 mL NS
1 mL of 2.25% solution diluted in 5 mL NS
questions.explanation: Asthma and croup both get 0.5 mL of the 2.25% solution diluted in 2.5 mL NS and nebulized; the pediatric column is the same as adult.

questions.title: Racemic Epinephrine
questions.stem: How many times and how often may racemic epinephrine be repeated for croup?
questions.explanation: The nebulized dose may be repeated twice at 15 minute intervals, matching the drug's roughly 5 minute onset and 1-3 hour duration.

questions.title: Racemic Epinephrine
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of racemic epinephrine?
options: Nonselective alpha and beta agonist, bronchodilator
questions.explanation: Racemic epinephrine is a nonselective alpha and beta agonist used as a bronchodilator; nebulized alpha effect shrinks mucosal edema in the subglottis, which is why it works in croup.

questions.title: Racemic Epinephrine
questions.stem: Which of these is an adverse reaction to racemic epinephrine?
questions.explanation: Beta stimulation produces tremor, tachycardia, nervousness and a rise in blood pressure; seizures and paradoxical bronchospasm are also listed.

questions.title: Racemic Epinephrine
questions.stem: What is the listed onset of nebulized racemic epinephrine?
questions.explanation: Onset is about 5 minutes with a 1-3 hour duration, which is why the repeat interval is 15 minutes rather than immediate re-dosing for a child still working to breathe.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: What is the IV rocuronium dose for paralysis during RSI?
questions.explanation: RSI paralysis is 1 mg/kg IV, with a 100 mg ceiling, and the pediatric column is the same as adult. 1.8 mg/kg is the IM equivalent.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: What is the IM rocuronium dose for paralysis during RSI?
questions.explanation: When given IM for RSI the dose rises to 1.8 mg/kg to overcome slower absorption. The separate 2 mg/kg IM dose applies to the combative patient without IV access.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: What is the maximum rocuronium dose for RSI paralysis?
questions.explanation: Both the RSI dose and the maintenance dose are capped at 100 mg, so a 120 kg patient still receives 100 mg rather than 120 mg.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: What is the rocuronium dose to maintain paralysis after intubation?
questions.explanation: Maintenance is half the intubating dose, 0.5 mg/kg, repeatable PRN with the same 100 mg ceiling. Paralysis without ongoing sedation is never acceptable.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: What is the adult rocuronium dose for a combative patient without IV access when succinylcholine is contraindicated?
questions.explanation: This extreme flight-safety situation uses 2 mg/kg IM — higher than the 1.8 mg/kg RSI IM dose — and carries no pediatric standing order.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: In which patients is rocuronium the paralytic agent of choice?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium is the paralytic of choice under 10 years of age, avoiding the bradycardia and hyperkalemia risks of succinylcholine in young children.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: What is the pharmacologic category of rocuronium?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium is a non-depolarizing blocker; it competes with acetylcholine at the motor end plate, an effect reversible by acetylcholinesterase inhibitors such as neostigmine.

questions.title: Rocuronium
questions.stem: What is the listed duration of rocuronium paralysis?
questions.explanation: Onset is 1 minute with a duration of 30 or more minutes — long enough that sedation must be running before the patient regains movement.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: What is the sodium bicarbonate dose for hyperkalemia?
questions.explanation: Hyperkalemia is treated with 1 mEq/kg IV, same as adult for pediatrics, repeatable if ECG changes or arrest persist in at-risk patients. 2 mEq/kg belongs to salicylate or barbiturate overdose.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: What is the maximum sodium bicarbonate dose for hyperkalemia?
questions.explanation: The 1 mEq/kg hyperkalemia dose is capped at 50 mEq — one amp. 100 mEq appears only for a QRS over 160 ms in TCA overdose.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: What is the sodium bicarbonate dose for salicylate or barbiturate overdose?
questions.explanation: Salicylate and barbiturate overdose use 2 mEq/kg IV followed by an infusion; alkalinizing the urine traps the drug and speeds elimination.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: What sodium bicarbonate infusion follows the initial dose in salicylate or barbiturate overdose?
options: 150 mEq (3 amps) in 850 mL D5W at 250 mL/hr
150 mEq (3 amps) in 850 mL D5W at 200 mL/hr
150 mEq (3 amps) in 850 mL NS at 250 mL/hr
50 mEq in 1000 mL D5W at 250 mL/hr
questions.explanation: The infusion is three amps (150 mEq) in 850 mL of D5W run at 250 mL/hr. The 200 mL/hr rate belongs to the adult TCA overdose infusion.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: An adult in TCA overdose has a QRS of 120 ms. What is the adult sodium bicarbonate bolus?
questions.explanation: A QRS over 100 ms in TCA overdose gets 50 mEq IVP in the adult column; the dose doubles to 100 mEq only once the QRS exceeds 160 ms.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: An adult in TCA overdose has a QRS of 180 ms. What is the adult sodium bicarbonate bolus?
questions.explanation: A QRS over 160 ms signals severe sodium channel blockade and gets 100 mEq IVP — two amps — rather than the 50 mEq used for a QRS over 100 ms.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: In TCA overdose, above what heart rate is a sodium bicarbonate bolus given?
questions.explanation: A heart rate over 140 is one of the listed triggers for a bolus, alongside QRS widening, seizures and hypotension. The 160 figure refers to QRS duration, not rate.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: How is the adult sodium bicarbonate infusion started in TCA overdose?
options: 50 mEq bolus, then infuse at 200 mL/hr
50 mEq bolus, then infuse at 250 mL/hr
1 mEq/kg bolus, then infuse at 200 mL/hr
100 mEq bolus, then infuse at 200 mL/hr
questions.explanation: After mixing 150 mEq in 850 mL D5W, the adult gets a 50 mEq bolus and the infusion runs at 200 mL/hr. If D5W is not available, boluses alone are used.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: A pediatric TCA overdose patient has a QRS of 180 ms. What sodium bicarbonate bolus is given?
questions.explanation: Pediatric dosing mirrors the adult pattern but weight-based: a QRS over 160 ms gets 2 mEq/kg IVP capped at 100 mEq, while QRS over 100 ms, HR over 140, seizures or hypotension each get 1 mEq/kg capped at 50 mEq.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: At what rate is the adult sodium bicarbonate infusion run for entrapment?
questions.explanation: After an NS bolus, three amps in 850 mL D5W are infused at 250 mL/hr to buffer the acid and potassium load released when a crushed limb is freed. The weight-based 5 mL/kg/hr rate is pediatric.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: At what rate is the pediatric sodium bicarbonate infusion run for entrapment?
questions.explanation: The same 150 mEq in 850 mL D5W mixture is run at 5 mL/kg/hr in children, not exceeding the adult rate of 250 mL/hr.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: Which risk limits sodium bicarbonate use in pediatric patients?
questions.explanation: The contraindications line names pediatric patients because bicarbonate may cause cerebral edema, so pediatric use is weighed carefully even though weight-based doses are listed.

questions.title: Sodium Bicarbonate
questions.stem: When is sodium bicarbonate indicated during cardiac arrest?
options: Only for suspected hyperkalemia or TCA overdose
questions.explanation: Routine administration in arrest is not indicated; it is reserved for arrests where hyperkalemia or TCA overdose is the suspected cause. The warnings add that it is rarely indicated in DKA.
